subject: SOC2: compact admin activity slice & delivery checkpoint
messages:
From: Veritas Audit <audits@veritas-audit.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: emma.clarke@helixpharma.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: SOC2 request — minimal admin-activity extract for control testing

Hi Kimberly,

Quick intro: I’m Sam from Veritas (external SOC2 assessor) — Helix has asked us to validate administrative activity logs for the period Apr 1–Jun 30, 2025. For the first pass we need a compact, auditable slice (not the full dataset) to validate event types, timestamps, user identifiers, and custody metadata.

Specifically we need:
- a compact extract containing: event_id, timestamp (UTC), actor_id, action_type, target_resource, ip_address, request_id, manifest_hash
- proof of custody: signed manifest, checksum, and transfer audit (S3 presigned or SFTP delivery)
- retention metadata: when each event will be purged/archived and the canonical retention policy that applied

Can you confirm:
1) whether Redwood can produce a compact JSONL or Parquet slice with the above fields and a signed manifest
2) typical delivery options (SFTP v. presigned S3) and ETA for a sample slice (<= 48 hours preferred)

If easier, we can schedule a 30-min tech call. Thanks — we want a small sample to avoid long transfer times for our first validation.

Best,
Sam Reed
Senior Auditor, Veritas Audit
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Veritas Audit <audits@veritas-audit.com>
Cc: emma.clarke@helixpharma.com, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 request — minimal admin-activity extract for control testing

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a compact extract and signed manifest. Details/choices below; I attached a one-page manifest example and the compact slice schema for reference.

Delivery formats we support for compact slices:
- JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) — easy human-readable; includes manifest with SHA256 checksums per file
- Parquet — columnar, smaller on wire for repeated fields (we typically recommend for >50k rows)

Custody & signing:
- We produce a manifest.json that includes file-level checksums, UTC generation timestamp, and signing metadata (KMS key id that signed the manifest). We can also provide a detached PKCS7 signature if your process requires it.

Retention metadata we will include for each event in the manifest: source_table, original_ingest_ts, retention_policy_id, scheduled_purge_ts, and redaction_mark (if any).

Transfer options:
- Presigned S3 URL (preferred for automation) — we include a transfer log entry with URL creation time and IP used to upload
- SFTP — available; we'll provide username + key and attach transfer.md with host/fingerprint
- Optional: secure ShareFile link if Helix requires an internal-controlled transfer portal

ETA for a small canary slice (up to 10,000 events): 24–36 hours from sign-off. Full scoped slice (customer-defined window) depends on timebox and jurisdictional redactions.

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm format (JSONL or Parquet) and delivery preference
- Confirm the sample window (we can do a rolling sample: 2k events from each month Apr/May/Jun)
- Decide whether you want the detached signature or KMS signing metadata only

I’ll loop in Ben for manifest custody and chain-of-custody checks.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: admin-activity-sample-manifest.json (stub), compact-slice-schema.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Veritas Audit <audits@veritas-audit.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, emma.clarke@helixpharma.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 request — minimal admin-activity extract for control testing

Adding a quick operational note from the handoff side:
- We recommend JSONL for the initial canary since it’s easier for your tooling to spot-check fields. Parquet is fine once schema is finalized.
- For the sample we’ll include a manifest with: generation_ts (UTC), producer_node_id, sha256 per file, total_records, and a custody_token (opaque id we log in our audit ledger).
- Transfer checksum verification: we will run a PGP/sha256 verification on delivery and emit a transfer event in our export audit ledger (we can provide that ledger row as a separate small CSV for your evidence bundle).

Can we target delivery of the canary JSONL by Mon 2025-12-01 18:00 PST? If you confirm, I’ll start the slice job and request the presigned S3 put URL.

Ben Carter
Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Reed <audits@veritas-audit.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: emma.clarke@helixpharma.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 request — minimal admin-activity extract for control testing

Thanks — JSONL via presigned S3 works best for our automation. Canary window sounds good: 2k per month for Apr/May/Jun (total ~6k). Detached PKCS7 also requested so our legal team can attest signature provenance.

Please proceed with:
- Canary JSONL (fields listed in original email) + manifest.json (SHA256 checksums) + detached PKCS7 signature
- Presigned S3 PUT URL and expected object key (we will retrieve and verify)
- Transfer log row (CSV) with custody_token and upload_ts

Confirming Mon 2025-12-01 18:00 PST delivery is acceptable. Tech call not required for now.

Best,
Sam
Veritas Audit
